title: Temporal Slope Regression Detector for Canary & Shadow Traffic
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Current canary and shadow rollouts rely on point-in-time score thresholds for golden prompt sets which catch many regressions but miss gradual quality declines and high-variance cohorts. We need a detector that accounts for time-series behavior of eval scores (per-prompt and aggregated) and surfaces both sudden drops and sustained negative trends so the rollout conductor can auto-quarantine or pause before customer-visible regressions escalate.

Goal: Implement a Temporal Slope Regression Detector (TSRD) that computes robust slope and change-point signals for golden prompt score series, integrates per-customer baselines with hierarchical smoothing, ties into the rollout controller for safe automated responses, and exposes explainability artifacts in the Console. The system must be resilient to low-signal prompts and noisy short-lived blips while being sensitive to persistent degradations across canary/shadow streams.
acceptance_criteria: A deployable detector service that subscribes to eval-score streams for canary and shadow traffic and emits events to the rollout conductor API.
Detector produces per-prompt and aggregated signals: slope (score/time), EWMA, change-point p-value, and sample-weighted confidence intervals.
Integration test with synthetic regressions demonstrating >90% recall and <5% false-positive quarantine rate on a curated benchmark (golden+noisy prompts).
Dashboard in Console that shows time-series, top contributing prompts, and drift attribution for any detector event.
Auto-quarantine workflow: detector event causes canary weight to pause and sends a notification with a PR template and rollback suggestion; manual override paths available.
Unit and e2e tests, code review, and feature flag gate for gradual rollout to production tenants.
implementation_notes: Data sources: reuse existing eval ingestion pipeline (clickhouse/analytics events) and augment with precomputed per-request eval scores. If necessary, add a lightweight scorer lambda for fast golden-set evaluation against streamed responses.

Core detector computes for each prompt: rolling window mean (W=5-15 mins), EWMA (alpha configurable), and linear regression slope with heteroskedasticity-robust SE. Also run CUSUM and Bayesian online change-point as secondary signals.
Aggregate signals across a golden set by sample-weighted pooling and by cohort (customer id, region, model-variant). Apply hierarchical shrinkage to avoid over-reacting to small cohorts.

Hysteresis and cooldown: need configurable hysteresis windows (default 10m) and minimum sample counts (default 50 samples per prompt/aggregate) before auto-action. Low-signal prompts flagged to human queue rather than auto-quarantine.
Storage & retention: keep sliding summaries for 30 days; raw per-request traces follow existing retention. Provide API to fetch top N prompts contributing to a regression event.

Alerting: detector emits structured events (type, confidence, top prompts, rolling metrics) to the rollout conductor and to PagerDuty channel. Include runbook URL and link to pre-filled rollback PR template.
design_decisions: Use slope + change-point combination instead of single-threshold gating to detect both abrupt and gradual regressions.
Implement detector as a separate microservice to avoid coupling to rollout conductor and to permit independent scaling and feature experimentation.
Leverage hierarchical Bayesian smoothing for cohort baselines to reduce false positives on small customers.
Expose tuning knobs in Console (window size, alpha, slope thresholds) behind feature flags per-org. Maintain safe defaults for public tenants.
Prefer explainability: always include the minimal set of prompts that drove the event and small example responses for rapid triage.
monitoring_playbook: On detector event: rollout conductor pauses canary weight, creates incident with detector payload, and opens triage ticket with linked golden prompt diffs.
If event confidence > 0.95 and sample_count >= threshold: auto-quarantine route and revert to previous model variant after 3 failed confirmatory checks spaced by hysteresis.
If low-confidence: route to human-in-loop review (oncall + product owner) and add to escalation queue. Keep canary running but cap traffic at 10% until cleared.
Post-action validation: detector runs a short confirmatory check using independent holdout golden prompts and sends a pass/fail signal back to the conductor.
rollout_integration: API contract: detector -> rollout-conductor POST /v1/detector-events with payload {key, confidence, top_prompts, suggested_action}. rollout-conductor returns 200 and applies configured policy (pause/quarantine/notify).
Policy config: allow per-project policies (auto_quarantine: on|off, min_samples, confidence_threshold, cool_down_minutes). Store policy in config service.
Provide CLI and Console controls to manually accept/reject detector suggested actions. Record audit logs for any manual override.
Fallback path: detector includes recommended fallback model variant (if compatible by tokenizer/arch) to be used for instant rollback.
